content:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High cross-region latency + increased error rate for requests routed to 'eu-west-1' from us-east clients. Trigger: routing-policy mismatch detection. Summary: 18% 5xx spike for /generate, elevated p99 latency. Thread started 2265123456.

alice: acked, I'm oncall. Pinged infra and cloud support.

ben: seeing same in grafana — region_pin_count for eu-west jumped around 03:02 UTC, lots of stale route hits.

carla: confirmed customers hitting eu-west when geo IP says us-east. Repro steps: curl from edge probe in us-east returns A record pointing to eu edge IP.

dinesh: running quick checks — traceroute from our probe shows path to eu edge via global anycast, looks like a DNS cache at provider edge holding old answer.

alice: possible root causes: routing policy rollout last night, TTL not lowered on switch, plus edge DNS caching. Immediate plan: 1) apply emergency routing override to force us-east pin; 2) shorten DNS TTL where possible; 3) push fallback route to internal LB.

eva: I've opened ticket with cloud-support (INC-9271). They see heavy negative cache retention on their resolver fleet for our zone. They recommend a spoofed SOA refresh + incremental TTL tweak.

infra-bot: runbook invoked: runbook/geo-pin-drift -> step 1 apply regional override.

alice: executing override now. Command:```
infractl route set --service inference --match geo=us-east --pin-region us-east --force
```

ben: infractl returned success, propagation announced to control plane.

carla: started active canary traffic to us-east. curl probe results:```
> curl -sI https://inference.redwood/api/health -H 'X-Test-Probe: us-east'
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Region: us-east
X-Route-Policy: override
```

dinesh: good — but dns still returning eu IPs from some public resolvers. Might be a mix of caches. We need TTL manipulation.

alice: pushing TTL change to 30s for our geo-zone. Command:```
dnsctl update-zone inference.redwood --record @ --ttl 30
```

infra-bot: DNS update submitted, change id dns-2265-ttl30. Cloud-support: will watch propagation.

cloud-support: we see the DNS change. Some edge resolvers will respect shorter TTL after refresh, but there will be residual cached entries until they expire. Suggest temporary HTTP-level redirect from eu edge to us-east for matching client IP ranges as stopgap.

ben: spinning up a redirect rule on eu edge:```
edgectl route add --from-region eu-west --match client_geo=us-east --action redirect --to-region us-east --ttl 60
```

carla: rule applied. Monitoring for feedback loop.

alice: updating customer impact matrix: impacted customers ~4% of traffic, mostly low-volume web SDKs with long-lived DNS. Customer visible symptom: occasional high-latency requests or 5xx when eu nodes overloaded. No data loss reported.

dinesh: running quick healthcheck against affected customers — adding a metric tag 'geo_mismatch' for filtering. Query:```
SELECT count(*) FROM request_logs WHERE tag='geo_mismatch' AND hour > now()-1h
```

ben: metric shows 3200 events in last 30m, concentrated on three ASNs in us-east.

eva: paging customer success for heads-up to large customers on those ASNs. cs-team pinged.

alice: good. Next: block to mitigate immediate impact is done (override + redirect + TTL). Now we need to root cause fix: investigate why routing-policy rollout left stale pins + why control-plane didn't lower TTL during rollout. Assigning follow-ups:
- dinesh: dig into rollout job logs and pin reconciliation, check commit 7a9c3b in routing-service.
- ben: add additional telemetry to routing-policy agent to emit pin-change events with before/after TTL.
- carla: coordinate with cloud-support on resolver cache behavior and ask for edge purge options.

dinesh: starting investigation. Preliminary: reconciliation loop skipped due to rate limiter misconfig in 7a9c3b; pins remained at previous priority.

cloud-support: we can run a targeted DNS cache purge for the zone, but it may take ~2-3 min per POP and might impact other services. Confirm?

alice: do purge for affected POPs in us-east and eu-west POPs that are caching. Approve.

cloud-support: purge in progress.

infra-bot: purge complete for POPs: iad1, ord1, lax1, cdg1.

carla: after purge, public resolvers show updated A records to us-east. Probes successful.

ben: metrics returning to baseline; p99 latency down from 2.1s to 220ms, error rate dropping.

alice: status update to execs drafted: "We observed cross-region routing drift due to a routing-policy rollout that didn't reconcile pins because of a rate-limiting regression. Emergency override, DNS TTL reduction, and targeted cache purge restored correct routing. Customer impact limited to ~4% traffic; mitigations applied; follow-up remediation in progress." I'll post on #incidents-summary in 10 min.

eva: CS sent notices to affected customers with workaround notes and the contact for escalations.

dinesh: digging deeper — found the rate limiter threshold for the reconciliation worker was set to 0.5 rps in prod by mistake in commit 7a9c3b; intended was 50 rps. Filing PR to revert and adding unit tests.

ben: I'll add a gating test to CI that deploys a simulated policy roll and asserts pin counts change within 60s.

carla: recommended postmortem outline: timeline, root cause (config regression), mitigation steps, testing gaps, action items (rollback commit, CI test, expanded telemetry, fail-safe TTL behavior), ETA for remediation.

alice: handoff to evening oncall (eva) at 2265123700. Handoff notes: emergency override still present, TTL 30s, redirect rule active, cloud-support purge done, root cause identified, fix PR in review. Watch metrics for next 3 hours and be ready to revert override once fix deploys.

eva: acked, I'll monitor. Please add me to the PR review and give me the rollback command.

alice: rollback command (if needed):```
infractl route revert --service inference --rollback-to tag=pre-2265-rollback
```

ben: leaving a link to dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/shared/geo-routing-incident-2265123456

carla: uploading packet captures and probe traces to incident ticket INC-2265123456.

infra-bot: deployment pipeline triggered for PR 2345, env=prod, change=rate-limiter-threshold-fix.

alice: thanks team. I'll post final summary after PR merges. :thumbsup: :eyes:

eva: monitoring, will escalate if anything changes.

incidents-bot: incident status -> mitigated; next state: monitoring.
